address: Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Phường 1, TP. Mỹ Tho, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
w: One of five eateries certified 'Quán hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho uy tín, chất lượng 2024' by Tiền Giang province — the definitive stop for hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho, the dry or soup rice-noodle dish built on chewy Gò Cát noodles, clear pork-and-dried-squid broth and a scatter of toppings. A long-running, no-frills local institution.
dish: hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho (Mỹ Tho rice-noodle soup)

address: TP. Mỹ Tho, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
w: Another of the five province-certified Mỹ Tho hủ tiếu houses (2024), this one specialising in the fish version — hủ tiếu cá — with sweet snakehead fish over the same trademark Mỹ Tho rice noodles. A local favourite that shows the dish beyond its standard pork form.

address: 188 Trần Hưng Đạo, Phường 1, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
w: A 50-year-old Sa Đéc noodle counter (open since 1968) famous for a MSG-free, bone-simmered Chinese-style broth and the silky rice noodles made from Sa Đéc's century-old flour village. Bowls have long started at almost nothing; go at lunch to beat the morning and evening crush.
dish: hủ tiếu Sa Đéc (Sa Đéc rice-noodle soup)

address: TP. Bến Tre, Bến Tre, Vietnam
w: The signature edible souvenir of the 'coconut land'. Thanh Long, founded 1970 by Nguyễn Thị Vinh — whose portrait on the wrapper became a symbol of Bến Tre — is one of the province's landmark coconut-candy brands, cooking and cutting the chewy caramel by hand and exporting to the US and Australia. Try it warm off the tray at a working workshop.

address: 86/38 Lý Tự Trọng, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
w: The best-known address for bánh cống, Cần Thơ's Khmer-origin fritter — a deep tube-mould of rice batter, mung bean and a whole shrimp fried golden and crisp, eaten with herbs and sweet-sour fish sauce. A cheap, beloved late-afternoon Tây Đô snack down a small alley off Lý Tự Trọng.

address: 17 Đại Lộ Hòa Bình, P. Tân An, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
w: Cần Thơ's most famous house for nem nướng Cái Răng — grilled pork balls seared over charcoal and rolled at the table with bánh hỏi, herbs, green banana, starfruit and pickled lemongrass in soft rice paper, dipped in a sweet-savoury sauce. A city institution on Hòa Bình boulevard.
dish: nem nướng Cái Răng (grilled pork rolls with bánh hỏi)

n: Bánh Tét Lá Cẩm Nhà Họ Huỳnh
address: Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, P. Bình Thủy, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
w: The Bình Thủy family lò that invented Cần Thơ's purple bánh tét — matriarch Huỳnh Thị Trọng (bà Sáu Trọng) first soaked the sticky rice in lá cẩm (magenta-plant) juice, wrapping it around mung bean, pork fat and salted egg. Now made by three-plus generations, it was named among Vietnam's Top 100 dishes/specialties (2017).
dish: bánh tét lá cẩm (magenta-leaf sticky-rice log)
